histories.openingDialogue: PIP: 'The village shut its gates before the office grew through them. Now the wolf wants a badge, and the sea has taken Char.' SCYLLA: 'I saw her at the anchor. Please do not turn that into a password.'
histories.continuity: The sealed village still owes a hearing to outsiders; the original Char died at the tide gate, with no implied return.

histories.openingDialogue: PIP: 'We kept the forest doors closed. The commuters kept theirs closed too, because someone sealed the tide gate.' OREN: 'Then our rescue plan starts with two locked lists.'
histories.continuity: The village's sealed witness policy and stranded commuters both require separate remedies; Char survived.

histories.openingDialogue: PIP: 'We called the empty district safe to flood. The wolf calls an empty office safe to burn. I dislike how familiar that sounds.' OREN: 'I have names from both places.'
histories.continuity: The sealed village cannot cite the ruined district as uninhabited; Char survived the diversion.

histories.openingDialogue: PIP: 'We opened Briar to witnesses. Then the tide gate opened and Char died. A good door can still exact a terrible price.' SCYLLA: 'Tell the wolf that before it calls this a victory.'
histories.continuity: Briar's witnesses can help evacuate the office but cannot rewrite the original Char's witnessed death.

histories.openingDialogue: PIP: 'Briar welcomed the people with stories. Earth's gate did not let its commuters out. We will need more than a friendly sign.' OREN: 'I can count everyone who is still missing.'
histories.continuity: The open witness network can support the rescue, but the stranded commuter debt remains; Char survived.

histories.openingDialogue: PIP: 'Our witnesses found a way through the trees. They also found families in the district everyone called abandoned.' OREN: 'I have the evacuation count and the missing count. Neither is zero.'
histories.continuity: Briar's open witness network knows the district was inhabited; Char survived but the flood's damage remains.

scenes.site: The House That Remembers / night-shift accounting floor
scenes.opening: The House That Remembers has acquired a fluorescent accounting department. Every time the clock punches midnight, the corridor folds back into a wolf road. A night-shift guard named Mara can prove which workers are trapped, but her badges have names that the wolf patrol considers stolen. Pip knows the wolf's oath language; the guard knows who is missing. Neither will surrender their list to the other. Behind the copy machine, a worker taps out a pair pattern on the door to keep the exit from vanishing.

dialogue.speaker: MARA
dialogue.line: My badge opens the stairwell. The wolf says it belongs to a person who never existed. I am standing right here.

dialogue.speaker: WOLF CAPTAIN
dialogue.line: A shift is not an oath. Tell me who will answer if these people cross my road.

dialogue.speaker: PIP
dialogue.line: We could ask them instead of deciding what their names mean. There is a door under that copier and it is getting smaller.

scenes.puzzle: Pair the two clock stamps that mark a real shift change, then choose who controls the names. The stamps are shown on Mara's timecard and on the corridor clock; no blind memory test or combat toll.

choices.label: Translate the shift roster into a temporary wolf-road oath
choices.visibleCost: Pip owes the wolf captain a future escort shift; the office cannot leave until the oath expires.
choices.reply: PIP: 'I will stand the night watch. Their time belongs to them.' MARA: 'Put that in writing, in both languages.'
choices.outcome: Mara checks each worker's consent and Pip translates the roster into a one-night promise. The wolf opens a guarded stair. Pip stays behind to honor the shift before catching up.
choices.laterCallback: e10 Morrow may cite the signed shift oath when the office's yōkai guardian demands proof of rest and safe departure.
choices.failureContinuation: If the wolf rejects a worker's name, Mara brings the worker to testify in person and Pip renews only the disputed line; the key remains recoverable.
choices.artSubject: Moth-eaten wolf-road oath over an office timecard, Pip and a night-shift guard at a fluorescent forest stair.

choices.label: Publish the number of trapped workers, not their private names
choices.visibleCost: The wolf captain demands an independent witness, delaying the rescue while the corridor contracts.
choices.reply: MARA: 'A head count, not a hunting list.' PIP: 'Then I will witness the door, not own it.'
choices.outcome: Mara records a consent-based count and the wolf accepts a neutral witness to each departure. The office keeps its private roster, but the evacuation takes an extra watch.
choices.laterCallback: e10 Morrow can reconcile the city's missing-worker count without exposing home addresses to the forest patrol.
choices.failureContinuation: If the witness misses the first bell, the guard shelters workers in the lit copy room until the second; no name is released without consent.
choices.artSubject: A giant paper head-count pinned between a wolf's claw and a copier, names blacked out, workers leaving by lamplight.

choices.label: Break the clock and evacuate before the wolf can demand a roster
choices.visibleCost: The timecard archive is destroyed, leaving Morrow without reliable evidence of who worked this shift.
choices.reply: PIP: 'We save the people first. The clock can argue with me later.' MARA: 'Then help me remember the names.'
choices.outcome: The corridor stops folding and the workers escape. Mara preserves spoken testimonies, but the damaged archive leaves an employment dispute for Earth to resolve.
choices.laterCallback: e10 Morrow must rebuild the employment record from worker testimony rather than rely on the destroyed timecards.
choices.failureContinuation: If the broken clock seals the main stair, Mara leads everyone through the signed emergency exit; the archive loss remains a cost.
choices.artSubject: Pip striking a forest-grown office clock while frightened workers hurry through a splintering fluorescent hallway.

scenes.replay: Exactly one irreversible decision and one fragment award. Reload restores the choice, cost and worker evidence; visiting the square alone awards nothing.

scenes.opening: The wolf road now runs beneath the sea. Roots of the House That Remembers have woven a dry pocket around a family who fled both a census and a flood. Scylla's tide chart predicts the next current, but the ink is washing toward the family's hidden address. Oren can build a bridge from office furniture, and a young refugee named Ren insists that no rescue map be sold after the crossing. The tide turns in three bells; choosing the quickest route might expose the shelter to every patrol above.

dialogue.speaker: REN
dialogue.line: We can swim. We cannot survive another map with our house marked on it.

dialogue.speaker: OREN
dialogue.line: I have six desks, two ropes, and three bells before the current reverses. We can save everyone if someone decides who sees the chart.

dialogue.speaker: SCYLLA
dialogue.line: The sea remembers the way out. It does not have to remember where you sleep.

scenes.puzzle: Use three visible tide marks and two matching root symbols to select a safe current. Incorrect order raises the water but opens a slower dry route; the scene never soft-locks a required fragment.

choices.label: Take a private escort along the chart's hidden current
choices.visibleCost: The tide rises while Oren escorts the family, leaving him unavailable for the next immediate encounter.
choices.reply: OREN: 'No address leaves this culvert. My axe can hold a rope as well as a gate.'
choices.outcome: The family reaches the high bank unseen. Oren sacrifices a tactical advantage to keep the route secret, and Ren takes custody of the original chart.
choices.laterCallback: e11 Char can honor Ren's custody claim when Vesper's refuge atlas appears in the coral palace.
choices.failureContinuation: If the tide runs early, Oren shelters the party on the House's dry landing until the next ebb. No patrol learns the address.
choices.artSubject: Hooded Oren holding a rope bridge through submerged House roots, Scylla guiding a family by a folded private tide chart.

choices.label: Dam the wolf road and open a public crossing
choices.visibleCost: The route is visible to patrols and the family must relocate their hidden shelter afterward.
choices.reply: SCYLLA: 'Everyone may cross. Nobody gets to keep a record of where Ren sleeps.' REN: 'Then help us move after.'
choices.outcome: A barricade of office desks diverts the current and strangers cross together. The family escapes, but Pip promises help relocating before the wolf patrol follows the new road.
choices.laterCallback: e11 Char hears Ren's relocation demand before deciding whether a public atlas can remain open.
choices.failureContinuation: If the dam breaks, Oren redirects evacuees to the high stair while the family carries its belongings to a new refuge.
choices.artSubject: Office desks stacked against a glowing seawater root tunnel, Pip and Scylla leading a public crossing while a wolf patrol approaches.

choices.label: Let the families operate a timed ferry with revocable access
choices.visibleCost: The crossing is slower and the group must leave supplies to maintain a ferry watch.
choices.reply: REN: 'We will decide when the ferry runs. We will also decide when it stops.' PIP: 'A road with an owner who can say no. I can live with that.'
choices.outcome: The refugees set a three-bell schedule and keep the route's key. Scylla lends a tide marker; the party loses supplies but gains a witness-controlled passage.
choices.laterCallback: e11 Char can cite the ferry's revocation rule when the palace registrar demands permanent access to Vesper's atlas.
choices.failureContinuation: If the first ferry misses the current, Ren keeps the family safe in the root pocket until the next marked bell; the charter is not voided.
choices.artSubject: Refugee-operated ferry of office doors in a sea-filled Briar culvert, Ren holding the bell and a revocable wooden pass.

scenes.replay: Exactly one irreversible decision and one fragment award. A missed tide puzzle changes rescue pacing, not whether the fragment can be earned.
